records.name: Peter Bressi Northeast Senior Center
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia senior center on Frankford Avenue with bingo, cards, exercise, computer lessons, trips, and a caseworker who helps with benefits.
records.what_you_do: Play cards or bingo, take an exercise class, learn computers, join a cooking event or trip, or talk with a caseworker about rent rebates, PACE, or housing.

schedule.text: Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

cost.text: The page lists no membership or program fees. Ask when you call.

first_step.how: Call (215) 831-2926 to ask about membership, or stop by during open hours and ask for a guided tour
first_step.basis: The page invites people to come in any time for a guided tour and gives a phone number to ask about joining
first_step.what_to_expect: The page does not describe a set first visit. Members are Philadelphia residents aged 60 and up, and the center offers cards, bingo, exercise, computer lessons, trips, and help from a caseworker with benefits, rent rebates, utilities, and housing.
first_visit_tips: Call first to ask about membership and the next tour
A secure parking lot is on site
Open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

records.notes: Membership is limited to Philadelphia residents aged 60 and up, which corrects the tier 1 open to public. The group's own news posts are from 2022 and 2023 only, so status rests on the city senior center listing. The site names no SEPTA stop, so none is recorded.

records.name: PAWS (Philadelphia Animal Welfare Society)
records.summary: A Philadelphia animal rescue with an Old City adoption center and two spay and neuter clinics. Volunteers can help at the shelter, and people can foster animals while they wait for homes.
records.what_you_do: Help with cat care, dog care, behind the scenes tasks, or adoption events, or open your home to foster animals until they are adopted.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts run through the year at the Old City adoption center and the Grays Ferry clinic, both open seven days a week, and at a PetSmart cat habitat on weekdays and weekends.

locations.label: Grays Ferry Spay/Neuter and Wellness Clinic

cost.text: Volunteering and fostering are unpaid. The group asks for donations.

requirements.gear: Nothing listed for volunteers. Foster homes provide a safe space and transport to the Grays Ferry clinic for medical care.

first_step.how: Pick a role on the volunteer page and submit the volunteer application, or fill out the online foster sign-up form and watch the onboarding video
first_step.basis: The volunteer page lists roles and how to apply, and the foster page explains the sign-up form and onboarding video
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers start with an application, and the site does not say what orientation includes or how long a shift lasts. Fostering comes with medical care paid by PAWS and supplies if you want them, but you provide a safe, separate space for cats and a way to keep dogs apart from resident pets. Typical foster stays run three to eight weeks or longer.
first_visit_tips: Check the volunteer page for current openings at each location
Call or email the location before you go: Old City 215-238-9901, Grays Ferry 215-298-9680
Foster questions go to foster@phillypaws.org

records.notes: The volunteer page says the Northeast clinic has no volunteer openings right now. Minimum age, background checks, and orientation details for volunteers are not stated on the site.

records.name: Philadelphia Dragon Boat Association
records.summary: The city's dragon boat racing club, founded in 1983, that trains on the Schuylkill and brings in newcomers through a rookie program that starts in June.
records.what_you_do: Paddle in early morning practices, try rookie sessions with loaner paddles and life jackets, and race in regattas.

schedule.text: High performance practices run five mornings a week, April through September, starting at 5:45 am. Rookie practices run once a week on a weeknight at 6 pm, starting in mid June, and the exact night is still to be set.

locations.label: Schuylkill River dock in Fairmount Park

cost.text: Dues are not listed on the site. Rookie practices supply loaner paddles, seat pads, and life jackets.

requirements.gear: Athletic clothing suited to the weather

first_step.how: Fill in the interest form on the recruiting page. The club says it replies within 72 hours, then come to a rookie practice in athletic clothing.
first_step.basis: The club runs rookie practices with loaner gear and explains how a newcomer starts, using an interest form and a reply time
first_step.what_to_expect: Rookie practices are a gentler entry than the early morning high performance sessions and focus more on technique. Loaner paddles, seat pads, and life jackets are provided, and rookie practice is once a week on a weeknight at 6 pm starting in mid June. The site does not say how long a practice lasts or whether you must swim.
first_visit_tips: Wear athletic clothes suited to the weather
Send the interest form first, since the club replies within 72 hours
Watch the recruiting page for the rookie night, which is still to be set

records.notes: The club's newest dated item is an April 2026 feature. Rookie night dates, swimming requirement, minimum age, and dues are not stated. Practice location is only given as the Fairmount Park dock on the Schuylkill, with no street address.

records.name: Philadelphia Furniture Workshop
records.summary: A woodworking school in Philadelphia that teaches furniture making through project classes, short tool courses and beginner courses. Classes are small and taught by experienced furniture makers.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner course, a learning series, a project class, or a short course on one tool or technique. The site also offers a newsletter sign-up for new classes.

schedule.text: Multi-week evening classes on Mondays and Thursdays, 6 to 9 pm, and weekend courses, 9 am to 4 pm, run through the year. New sessions are added as they are scheduled.

cost.text: Classes cost about $425 to $1,425 each, depending on length. Most fees include materials, and the site lists no drop-in fee.

requirements.gear: Most course fees include materials. Some courses link a recommended tool list.

first_step.how: Pick a beginner course or learning series from the class list, or sign up for the newsletter to hear when new classes open
first_step.basis: The site names beginner courses and a learning series for new woodworkers and says the classes are small and taught by experienced makers
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes are small and taught by experienced furniture makers. Multi-week classes meet once a week in the evening, and weekend courses run 9 am to 4 pm, with lunch brought from home on some. The site does not describe a first class or say which tools the school supplies.
first_visit_tips: Check the course list for the start date and the recommended tool list linked on each course
Bring your own lunch for the weekend courses that say so
Ask by email or phone about shop hours, since none are listed

records.notes: Several listed classes are not yet scheduled, and one is sold out. The site lists a June 2026 magazine feature as its newest dated item. Shop hours, accessibility, parking, and transit are not on the site.

records.name: Philadelphia Mineralogical Society
records.summary: Rock, mineral and fossil fans who meet each month for a guest speaker, take collecting trips and visit private collections, and hold a yearly show.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly talks, join collecting and collection-visit trips, and take part in the spring mineral show.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the second Thursday, doors open at 7 pm for social time and the program starts at 7:30 pm, in person or on Zoom.

cost.text: Membership cost is not listed on the site, and the site does not say whether guests pay.

first_step.how: Come to a public monthly meeting in person, or ask for the Zoom link through the society's website contact form
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to the public and the website explains how to get the Zoom link, but the site does not describe a beginner program
first_step.what_to_expect: Each meeting has a short business part, then a lecture or video presentation, with social time before it. Topics change from month to month and are listed on the site. The site does not say whether guests pay.
first_visit_tips: Arrive around 7 pm for social time
Use the website contact form to ask for the Zoom link if you want to join online
The in-person meetings are in Wayne, Delaware County, not in the city

records.notes: Venue is in Wayne (Delaware County), outside Philadelphia, and the site says the venue changed in January. The group is kept as publish because its name and reach are Philadelphia area and it welcomes online visitors, but the owner may want to decide whether out_of_area fits better. The site's join page returned a 404, so membership details are unknown.

records.name: Philadelphia Orchard Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that plants and cares for community orchards across Philadelphia, working with schools, churches, and community gardens. Anyone can help at its open work days.
records.what_you_do: Dig, plant, mulch, prune, and weed at orchard work days, and help with workshops and events.

schedule.text: Weekly Tuesday work days at the Learning Orchard at The Woodlands, a monthly open orchard afternoon, and seasonal planting days.

locations.label: POP Learning Orchard at The Woodlands

cost.text: No volunteer fee is listed for individuals.

first_step.how: Join the volunteer email list through the volunteer sign-up form, or register for a work day on the events page
first_step.basis: Work days need no experience, and the site explains how to join the volunteer list and register for a work day
first_step.what_to_expect: Work days are hands on, with digging, planting, mulching, pruning, and weeding at the orchard. The volunteer email list announces the work days, with more of them in spring and fall. The site does not say how long a work day lasts or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the volunteer email list so you hear about work days
Register on the events page for the work day you want
Ask the group what to wear, since the volunteer page does not say

records.notes: The volunteer page does not say what to wear, whether tools are provided, parking or transit, or accessibility for work days. Group volunteering is limited to small groups of 5 to 10 people. The FAQ page returned a 404.

records.name: Philadelphia's First Toastmasters Club (Club 541)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets online on Thursday evenings to practice speaking and leading meetings. Guests are welcome to visit before they decide to join.
records.what_you_do: Give short prepared speeches, take part in impromptu speaking rounds, and fill meeting roles on Zoom, with feedback from other members.

schedule.text: Thursday evenings on Zoom, around 7 pm, with upcoming meeting dates listed on the club site.

cost.text: Visiting a club meeting is free. The site does not show dues.

first_step.how: Join a Thursday meeting on Zoom using the link on the club site, or use the contact form to plan a first visit
first_step.basis: The club says guests are welcome, invites visitors to attend a meeting, and offers a contact form to plan a first visit
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is an evening on Zoom. Members give short prepared speeches, practice speaking without notes, and take turns running meeting roles, with feedback after each speech. The site does not describe a guest role, so ask ahead through the contact form.
first_visit_tips: Join five to ten minutes early
Ask through the contact form which meeting to attend and how to get the Zoom link
Confirm the start time, since the site lists both 6:45 pm and 7 pm

records.notes: The club's site gives both 6:45 pm and 7 pm start times, so confirm before attending. The Zoom meeting details on the site are left out of this record on purpose. Dues, guest roles, and language or accessibility options are not on the site.

notes: Seven groups from the batch were read. Two pages returned HTTP 404 and were skipped: the mineral society join page and the orchard FAQ. Peter Bressi's own news is dated 2022 and 2023, so its status rests on the city listing. The mineral society's in-person venue is in Wayne, Delaware County, outside the city, so the owner may want to rule on its verdict. No WebSearch was needed because each site had the pages required. Budget was not exhausted.
